newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Reprieve for Liberia warlord Kromah.
newsitem.headline: Reprieve for Liberia warlord Kromah.

text.p: West African peacekeepers dropped charges against Liberian warlord and presidential hopeful Alhaji Kromah on Friday after he apologised for keeping an illegal arms cache at his home after a disarmament deadline.

General Victor Malu, commander of the Nigerian-led ECOMOG force, said in a radio broadcast that he would asked the Liberian authorities to drop the case as well. At the same time, peacekeepers lifted a house arrest order on Kromah.

"I am requesting that charges against Alhaji Kromah be dropped over this matter and wish to state that a similar request is extended on behalf of those we found with arms and handed over the the Liberian authorities," he said.

Earlier on Friday Kromah, who had been under house arrest since March 7 after discovery of the arms, said he had not intended to use the arms and reiterated his support for the West African sponsored peace deal to end seven years of civil war.
"I wish to admit the error of having arms at my residence after the January deadline for disarmament," he told a news conference.
"The arms were never intended for any evil motives, rather they were intended for delivery to ECOMOG," Kromah said.
Malu portrayed the move as a gesture to help the peace process in Liberia, saying it should not be misunderstood.

"Let me categorically state and warn that this plea on our part should not be considered as a licence to believe that we will relent in our effort to rid this country of arms or a signal that we will allow people to hoard arms," he said.

Kromah, who hopes to contest the May 30 presidential election, was accompanied at the news conference by the ECOMOG chief of staff, Brigadier Abdoul One-Mohammed, and Liberia's justice minister, Peter Bonnor Jallah.
"I do not feel too big to apologise for the error and wish to assure you of my determination to help ensure the successful completion of the peace process," he said.
Kromah gave the news conference, his first public reaction to the affair, at his seaside residence in eastern Monrovia. ECOMOG tanks and troops began to withdraw after Malu spoke.
West African leaders brokered the peace deal, which followed a dozen failed accords, in Nigeria's capital Abuja last August.
Well over 150,000 people have been killed by the war.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847 and their descendants dominated the West African nation until a 1980 coup by the indigenous krahn ethnic group.
Rival faction leaders Charles Taylor, who launched the war in December 1989, and George Boley have also announced their intention to run for president.
